service: Correction of Birth Certificate (Spelling, First Name, Birth Date or Sex)
description: File a petition at the City Civil Registry to correct a misspelling, change a first name, or fix a wrong day or month of birth or a wrong sex on a birth certificate. Once approved, an annotation is added to the birth certificate to show the change.
whoMayAvail: Parents; the child (18 or older); the owner of the document (18 or older); or a representative with a Special Power of Attorney, such as a spouse, grandparent, sibling or legal guardian.

detailedRequirements.requirement: Wrong spelling: PSA Birth Certificate with the misspelling

Wrong spelling: 2 or more of: Baptismal Certificate; school record or diploma; Voter's Affidavit or Certification; GSIS/SSS record; PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG Member's Data; land titles; government-issued IDs

Wrong spelling: civil registry records of ascendants (parents, grandparents) or descendants (children, grandchildren); Birth Certificate and Marriage Certificate of the parents; Birth Certificates of siblings or children
Change of first name: PSA Birth Certificate with the wrong name
Change of first name: 2 or more of: school records or diploma; Voter's Affidavit or Certification; GSIS/SSS record; PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG Member's Data; land titles
Change of first name: Baptismal Certificate; Marriage Contract (if married); Police Clearance; NBI Clearance with the A.K.A. name; Certificate of Employment or Employer's Clearance

Wrong day or month of birth: PSA Birth Certificate with the wrong birthday; Baptismal Certificate; earliest medical records; elementary school records; Certificate of Employment or Affidavit of Non-Employment; NBI Clearance; Police Clearance
Wrong day or month of birth: newspaper publication of the petition once a week for 2 weeks, with Affidavit of Publication

Wrong sex: PSA Birth Certificate with the wrong sex; earliest medical records; original Baptismal Certificate; elementary school records; Certificate of Employment or Affidavit of Non-Employment; NBI Clearance; Police Clearance
Wrong sex: newspaper publication of the petition once a week for 2 weeks, with Affidavit of Publication
Wrong sex: medical certificate stating the petitioner has not undergone a sex change
Indigent petitioners (no filing fee): Certificate of Indigency
detailedRequirements.where_to_secure: City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO)

steps: Prepare the requirements for your type of correction.

File the petition at the City Civil Registry, Ground Floor, City Hall Annex Bldg., Gen. Luna St., Tuktukan. If you have moved, file a migrant petition with the civil registrar of the city or town where you now live.
Wait for approval (4 to 6 months). The approved change is shown as an annotation on the birth certificate.

quickInfo.fee: Born in Taguig: ₱1,000 (spelling) or ₱3,000 (first name, sex or birth date). Migrant petitioners or those not born in Taguig pay an extra ₱500 (spelling) or ₱1,000 (first name, sex or birth date). Free for indigent petitioners with a CSWDO Certificate of Indigency.

service: Delayed Registration of Certificate of Marriage
description: Register a marriage that was not registered within the deadline (15 days for marriages with a license, 30 days for PD 1083 and Art. 34 cohabitation marriages). Marriages more than 1 year late need extra documents.

detailedRequirements.requirement: Application form for Certificate of Marriage (4 copies, typewritten, no erasures)
Muslim attachment for Marriage (Muslims only, 4 copies)
Duly accomplished Affidavit for Delayed Registration
detailedRequirements.where_to_secure: Back of the application form for Certificate of Marriage

detailedRequirements.requirement: Original Marriage License
Original Affidavit of Cohabitation (couples living together for at least 5 years, Art. 34 of the Family Code; 4 copies)
Notarized request for the celebration of marriage in a place other than authorized by law (if the wedding was held outside a church or mosque; dated and notarized before the wedding)
Certificate of Registration of Authority to Solemnize Marriage (CRASM) of the solemnizing officer
Valid ID

For Muslim couples, the affidavit must state: the couple's details, the dates and place of marriage and the name of the imam/ustadz; that the marriage was solemnized under Presidential Decree No. 1083; and that the marriage was among Muslims or members of ethnic cultural communities and solemnized according to their customs
If more than 1 year late: latest PSA CENOMAR of the groom and bride (valid for 6 months)
If more than 1 year late: latest original PSA No Record/Negative Result for the Certificate of Marriage (valid for 1 year)
If more than 1 year late: certification with a certified true copy of the book record
detailedRequirements.where_to_secure: Church or Hall of Justice where the wedding was held

detailedRequirements.requirement: If more than 1 year late: picture of the couple at the wedding ceremony
If more than 1 year late: notarized Affidavit of Delayed Registration, signed by the groom, bride, solemnizing officer and two witnesses

steps: Prepare all original requirements and a valid ID, with 2 photocopies of each.

Submit them in person at the City Civil Registry, Ground Floor, City Hall Annex Bldg., Gen. Luna St., Tuktukan, Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM. The husband, wife, pastor, ustadz/imam or church clerk must appear personally, with a Special Power of Attorney (SPA) letter from the couple.
The Certificate of Marriage is released 10 days after posting.

service: Free Late Birth Registration (Mobile Birth Registration)
description: The City Civil Registry visits every barangay to offer free late birth registration to Taguig-born residents whose birth was never registered.
whoMayAvail: Taguig residents whose birth was not registered within 30 days. If you were born outside Taguig, the City Civil Registry coordinates with the city or town where you were born (out-of-town registration). If the parents are married, either parent may file. If they are not married, both parents must appear, unless one has died, is abroad, or left and abandoned the family. In that case the mother may register alone (the child uses the mother's surname), or the father may; the mother's mother may also register with an Affidavit of Guardianship. Applicants 18 and older may file for themselves; children aged 7–17 must come along.

detailedRequirements.requirement: Registration form for Certificate of Live Birth (COLB), typewritten or computerized, signed and notarized
Notarized Affidavit for Delayed Registration of Birth
Negative certification proving the applicant has no birth certificate yet
Certified true copy of the parents' Marriage Certificate (if parents are married)
Notarized Affidavit of Acknowledgment/Admission of Paternity and Affidavit to Use the Surname of the Father (if parents are not married)
Notarized Affidavit of Two Disinterested Persons who witnessed the birth
Certification from the Barangay Chairman of where the mother lived on the day of birth
Parent's National ID and another valid ID

Any 2 of: original Baptismal Certificate; Medical Certification or Immunization Card from the Health Center; certified true copy of Form 137 (ages 7–17); certified true copy of Voter's Registration (18 and above)

steps: Go to a Mobile Birth Registration site (check the City Civil Registry – City of Taguig Facebook page for the schedule) or to the City Civil Registry office, and get a Certificate of Live Birth (COLB) form.
Fill out the COLB (typewritten or computerized) and sign it. Fill out and sign the Affidavit for Delayed Registration of Birth at the back, then have the COLB notarized.
Bring the complete requirements to the registration site or the office. Mobile Birth Registration has only 300 slots, so come early; it may be postponed in bad weather.
Right after registering, you can get a certified photocopy of the birth certificate at the Records Section of the City Civil Registry. It costs ₱50 per copy.

quickInfo.fee: Free registration (you pay for notarization, barangay clearance and the PSA negative certification)

description: A death certificate states the time, place and cause of a person's death. This is how to register one with the City Civil Registry, whether the person died at home or in a hospital. Forms and other requirements are available at the City Civil Registry office.
whoMayAvail: Only the spouse, child, parent or a relative of the deceased may get the death certificate. Bring a valid ID or another document proving you are a relative.

detailedRequirements.requirement: Death in a hospital: typewritten death certificate form, with the cause of death and a completed embalmer's box
Death at home: 4 original copies of Municipal Form 103, filled out by the funeral parlor
Death at home: all medical records of the deceased and the deceased retrieval form signed by the health center
Transfer Permit (if needed)
detailedRequirements.where_to_secure: Sanitation Office, City Health Office (CHO) Room 5

detailedRequirements.requirement: For Muslims: an additional Municipal Form 103, signed by the imam
Medico-legal cases: as required by the health center or the City Health Office doctor
Valid ID or document proving you are a relative of the deceased

steps: Death in a hospital: (1) The hospital gives the typewritten death certificate form. (2) Bring the form to City Health Office (CHO) Room 5 for final review. (3) If needed, get a Transfer Permit from the Sanitation Office at CHO Room 5. (4) Register the death certificate at the City Civil Registry.

Death at home: (1) Get 4 original copies of Municipal Form 103 and have the funeral parlor fill them out. (2) Bring the form, all medical records and the deceased retrieval form signed by the health center to the barangay health center for an interview. (3) Bring the form, the cause of death and other documents to the City Health Office (CHO) for final review. (4) If needed, get a Transfer Permit from the Sanitation Office at CHO Room 5. (5) Register the death certificate at the City Civil Registry.
The City Civil Registry, Ground Floor, City Hall Annex Bldg., Gen. Luna St., Tuktukan is open Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and Saturday and Sunday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM for death certificates.
